chunks: And he, peace be upon him, said:
Ten things from a dead animal are considered pure: the horn, the hoof, the bone, the tooth, the rennet, the milk, the hair, the wool, the feathers, and the eggs.

key_terms.الْإِنْفَحَةُ: rennet found in the stomach and used in curdling milk
key_terms.الْمَيْتَةِ: a dead animal not slaughtered according to the law; carrion
key_terms.ذَكِيَّةٌ: treated here as pure and not subject to the impurity ruling of carrion

ai.seo_question: Which parts of a dead animal are considered pure in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling that ten specific parts or substances from a dead animal are treated as pure. It is significant in fiqh discussions of taharah and najasah, especially regarding what may remain ritually pure despite coming from carrion.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Ten things from a dead animal are considered pure: the horn, the hoof, the bone, the tooth, the rennet, the milk, the hair, the wool, the feathers, and the eggs."
